final_text:
Returned hints for `https://docs.google.com/document/` / `compose-draft`:

1. Example: Google Docs one-page brief with a table
   Name the document, add headed sections, then insert a table from the Insert menu and fill it cell by cell with Tab.
   - Insert, then Table, opens a size grid: hover to the size you want, then click
   - Tab moves to the next cell; Tab in the last cell adds a row, so skip it there
   - Type the header row first, then the data rows
   - Check that the table fits the page width before moving on
   - Wait for the saved indicator
   pitfalls: stray-empty-row, untitled-document

2. Example: Google Docs meeting notes from a template
   Create a document, name it, insert the built-in meeting notes template and replace each placeholder with the real date, attendees, agenda and action items.
   - Name the document in the title box at the top left, then press Enter
   - A new empty page offers template chips; Insert, then Building blocks, has the same templates
   - Replace every placeholder before you finish
   - Keep action items as a bulleted list with an owner and a date
   - Docs saves by itself: wait for the saved indicator
   pitfalls: untitled-document, placeholder-left-behind

3. Example: Google Docs weekly status report with headings and bullets
   Write a short status report with a title and three headed sections (done, next, blockers) with bullet lists. Pick headings from the styles menu and check the outline panel.
   - Choose headings from the styles menu; that works in every account
   - If Markdown shortcuts are on, # and - may convert by themselves: look at the result before retyping
   - The outline panel lists the headings that took effect
   - Use one bullet per item and keep each item to one line
   - Wait for the saved indicator before leaving
   pitfalls: markdown-shortcut-surprise, untitled-document

Note: Entries titled Example: are starter examples, not verified site knowledge.
